name: Trust entire account root
fix: Trust specific role ARNs, or add aws:PrincipalArn / aws:PrincipalTag conditions.
risk: Any over-privileged identity in the trusted account can assume this role.
about: Trusting <account>:root delegates the decision to every principal in that account that has sts:AssumeRole on this role (including '*' policies).

name: Cross-acct trust without ExternalId
fix: Add StringEquals sts:ExternalId = <unique value agreed with the third party>.
risk: Confused-deputy: any customer of the third party can make it assume your role.

name: KMS grants to external accounts
fix: Retire grants that are not needed; prefer key-policy statements with conditions you can audit.
risk: Grants bypass the key policy and are easy to forget; another account can decrypt your data.

name: Permissions boundary missing (priv role)
fix: Attach a permission boundary that denies IAM/Organizations changes outside approved paths.
risk: Any escalation through this role is unbounded.
about: The role can change IAM / pass or assume roles, and nothing caps its maximum permissions.

name: Account password policy is weak
fix: Update the password policy (iam:UpdateAccountPasswordPolicy); it applies at the next password change.
risk: Weak console passwords are easier to guess, steal or replay.
about: GetAccountSummary shows root access keys or a root password without MFA.

name: Root account has keys or no MFA
fix: Delete root access keys and enable (hardware) MFA on root.
risk: One shared credential with unlimited privilege and no per-user attribution.
about: GetAccountSummary shows root access keys or a root password without MFA.

name: NHI can modify SCP/Organizations
fix: Restrict Organizations write actions to a break-glass role in the management account.
risk: Removing SCP guardrails or detaching accounts disables preventive controls org-wide.

name: NHI without owner tag
fix: Tag the workload (and its role) with owner / team; enforce with a tag policy or SCP.
risk: Nobody is accountable for the identity's permissions, rotation or decommissioning.
about: Neither identities.owner nor an owner/team tag is set.

name: Missing SCP guardrails
fix: Attach a baseline SCP denying these actions (with an exception for a break-glass role).
risk: A compromised NHI can disable detection or leave the organization's controls.

name: Inline policies on NHI
fix: Convert to customer-managed policies managed by IaC.
risk: Inline policies bypass managed-policy review and versioning; drift goes unnoticed.

name: Account BPA not enabled
fix: Enable all four account-level S3 Block Public Access settings.
risk: Any bucket can become public through a policy or ACL change.

name: Missing RCP for resource exposure
fix: Attach an RCP denying these actions when aws:PrincipalOrgID != your org (with service-principal exceptions).
risk: A single mis-written resource policy can expose data to any AWS account.

name: Shadow NHI created outside governance
fix: Recreate the identity through IaC, or add the creator to the approved list if legitimate.
risk: Shadow identities skip review, tagging and least-privilege controls.

name: NHI can disable security logging
fix: Remove these actions; protect logging with an SCP that denies them for everyone except a break-glass role.
risk: An attacker using this identity can stop or delete the CloudTrail audit log and its log groups to hide what it does.

name: No recent use of the roles that trust a login provider
fix: Confirm the federation is no longer needed, then remove the trust from the roles and delete the provider.
risk: An unused trust is still an open door; nobody notices if an attacker starts using it.

name: SAML signing certificate about to expire
fix: Rotate the IdP signing certificate and upload the new metadata (iam:UpdateSAMLProvider).
risk: An expiring certificate signals an unmaintained provider; rotating late can break sign-in when the IdP changes keys.

name: OIDC provider certificate fingerprint is out of date
fix: Verify the provider's certificate and update the thumbprint list (iam:UpdateOpenIDConnectProviderThumbprint). If issuer and JWKS hosts differ, include both thumbprints.
risk: Sign-ins can break, or the trust may point at the wrong certificate, weakening who AWS believes the login provider is.

name: SAML logins allowed without encryption
fix: Enable assertion encryption at the IdP and set AssertionEncryptionMode=Required (iam:UpdateSAMLProvider).
risk: Unencrypted assertions can expose user attributes to anyone who can read them in transit or in browser logs.

name: Federated login session allowed to last too long
fix: Lower MaxSessionDuration on the role to your limit (1 hour is the AWS default).
risk: If a federated session is stolen, a longer duration gives the attacker more time before it expires.

name: Role trusts more than one login provider
fix: Keep one provider per role where possible, or give each provider its own role with matching sub / aud conditions.
risk: Every extra login provider is another way in; a weak provider becomes a path to the same role.

name: CodeBuild role + PassRole escalation
fix: Scope iam:PassRole to the specific roles builds need, with iam:PassedToService.
risk: Anyone who controls the build (buildspec, dependency) escalates to the most privileged role in the account.

name: CI/CD OIDC role deploys to prod
fix: Limit sub to repo:<org>/<repo>:environment:production (with required reviewers) or ref:refs/heads/main.
risk: A pull request or feature branch can run with production deploy permissions.

name: Secrets in image layers
fix: Rotate the secrets, rebuild without them (multi-stage builds, build secrets), delete affected tags.
risk: Anyone who can pull the image (or any old tag) can extract the credentials.

name: Deploy role over-privileged
fix: Scope the deploy role to the stacks/services it deploys; use permission boundaries for roles it creates.
risk: Pipeline compromise (malicious dependency, PR) yields broad account access.

name: CI/CD with static long-lived keys
fix: Switch to OIDC federation (e.g. GitHub Actions -> AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity) and delete the keys.
risk: Keys stored in CI secrets leak through logs, forks and compromised runners and never expire.

name: GitHub OIDC role broad
fix: StringEquals token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud = sts.amazonaws.com and sub = repo:<org>/<repo>:<ref|environment>.
risk: Workflows in other repositories (or other GitHub orgs) can assume the role.

name: Privileged role assumable by low-trust
fix: Restrict the trust policy to the specific automation roles that need it; add MFA/ExternalId/PrincipalOrgID conditions.
risk: Privilege jump: a weak identity becomes privileged with one AssumeRole call.

name: Policy version escalation
fix: Remove these actions from workload roles; restrict policy management to the IaC pipeline role.
risk: Any principal with the policy attached (including this identity) can be made administrator.

name: Self policy modification
fix: Remove IAM write actions on the role itself; use a permission boundary that denies IAM changes.
risk: The workload can grant itself administrator access at any time.

name: CreateRole + AttachPolicy escalation
fix: Remove these actions, or require a permission boundary on created roles (iam:PermissionsBoundary condition).
risk: Privilege escalation to administrator through a newly created role.

name: Toxic permission combination
fix: Remove the actions or scope them to specific resources; deny them in a permission boundary.
risk: Each primitive lets the identity act as another, usually more privileged, principal.

name: Deep role-chaining path
fix: Break the chain: restrict sts:AssumeRole to the roles the workload needs and tighten trust policies.
risk: Deep chains hide the real origin of actions in CloudTrail and widen effective access.
about: Assume-role path:

name: End-to-end exfiltration path
fix: Remove internet exposure or the data permissions; scope data access to specific resources; add VPC endpoint policies.
risk: One exploit of the exposed workload leads directly to bulk data theft.

name: High blast-radius identity
fix: Split responsibilities across smaller roles and remove assume-role paths to privileged roles.
risk: Compromise of this identity affects a large part of the account.

name: PassRole + compute-create combo
fix: Scope iam:PassRole to specific role ARNs with iam:PassedToService; remove unused create permissions.
risk: Privilege escalation to any role that can be passed (often admin).

name: Cross-account lateral movement
fix: Remove cross-account sts:AssumeRole unless required; scope it to specific role ARNs with ExternalId/conditions.
risk: Compromise of this workload spreads to other accounts.

name: Exposure-to-privilege path
fix: Remove the exposure or the path (assume-role permission / trust) to the privileged role.
risk: Internet exploit -> privileged AWS access.

name: Role can remove or weaken its own permissions boundary
fix: Deny iam:DeleteRolePermissionsBoundary / PutRolePermissionsBoundary on the role (in the boundary itself or an SCP).
risk: The boundary is only advisory: an attacker removes it, then uses the role's full policies.
about: The role has a permissions boundary and is allowed to delete or replace it.

name: Can assign a stronger Lambda execution role
fix: Scope iam:PassRole to specific roles with iam:PassedToService=lambda.amazonaws.com, and limit UpdateFunctionConfiguration.
risk: A low-privilege credential becomes the strongest role it can pass.
about: lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration plus iam:PassRole on \

name: Session Manager role over-privileged
fix: Keep the instance role to AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore + what the workload needs; restrict ssm:StartSession.
risk: ssm:StartSession on the instance becomes a privilege escalation to the instance role.
about: Anyone who can start a Session Manager session on the instance inherits this role:

name: Redshift role over-privileged
fix: Scope the role to the specific S3 prefixes / services the cluster uses (COPY/UNLOAD, Spectrum).
risk: SQL users who can run COPY/UNLOAD use this role: database access becomes broad AWS access.

name: SA cluster-admin + privileged IRSA
fix: Remove cluster-admin from the service account and scope the IRSA role to the workload's needs.
risk: Compromise of a single pod = full cluster control + privileged AWS access.

name: Wildcard resource (Resource:*)
fix: Scope Resource to the specific ARNs (or ARN prefixes) the workload works on.
risk: The workload can modify or delete resources it never touches, including other teams' data.

name: Broad IAM auth role
fix: Scope rds-db:connect to arn:aws:rds-db:<region>:<acct>:dbuser:<db-resource-id>/<specific-user>.
risk: The workload can log in as any database user (including admin users) of any IAM-auth database.

name: Service-linked role has customer-added permissions
fix: Remove the inline / customer-managed policies from the service-linked role.
risk: An attacker who abuses the service plane gains the extra permissions too.
about: Customer-modifiable permissions were added to a role meant to carry only the AWS-managed service policy.

name: Execution role over-privileged
fix: Use AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy plus only the specific secrets/parameters the task needs; put app permissions on the task role.
risk: The execution role is available to the ECS agent on the host; extra permissions widen what a host compromise yields.

name: Private CA broadly permissioned
fix: Restrict acm-pca:IssueCertificate to specific CA ARNs and issuing pipelines; remove public/cross-account CA policy.
risk: Whoever can issue certificates can impersonate services and IAM Roles Anywhere workloads trusted by this CA.

name: Key without rotation enabled
fix: Enable automatic key rotation (EnableKeyRotation).
risk: Compromised key material stays valid for all future encryptions.
about: The customer-managed symmetric key does not rotate its key material.

name: Hardcoded secrets in task definition
fix: Rotate the secret; use the containerDefinitions 'secrets' field (Secrets Manager / SSM) instead of 'environment'.
risk: Task definitions are readable with ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition and keep every revision forever.

name: Workload using IAM user keys vs role
fix: Remove the keys from the workload and use its instance profile / task role / execution role (temporary credentials).
risk: Static keys never expire, are copied into code/config and bypass the workload's role boundary.

name: Secrets in bucket objects/state
fix: Rotate the secrets, remove them from objects (use remote state with encryption, Secrets Manager), restrict bucket access.
risk: Anyone who can read the bucket (or a backup of it) gets the credentials.

name: Unused access keys
fix: Deactivate the key now and delete it after confirming nothing depends on it.
risk: Unused active keys are unmonitored standing credentials; a leak goes unnoticed.

name: Plaintext secret in String parameter
fix: Rotate the secret and store it as SecureString with a customer-managed key (or in Secrets Manager).
risk: Plaintext secret readable without any KMS permission.
about: A credential-like value is stored unencrypted; anyone with ssm:GetParameter (and console users) can read it.

name: SecureString without CMK
fix: Re-encrypt with a customer-managed KMS key whose policy allows only the intended consumers.
risk: No separation between 'can read the parameter' and 'can decrypt it'.
about: The parameter is encrypted with alias/aws/ssm, whose key policy cannot be restricted: any principal with ssm:GetParameter can decrypt it.

name: Machine identity has a console password
fix: Delete the login profile (iam:DeleteLoginProfile).
risk: A console password is a second, human-style way in that nobody owns, rotates or protects with MFA.
about: A non-human IAM user has a login profile. Workloads only need programmatic access.

name: Unrenewed certificate past its rotation window
fix: Re-issue the certificate (prefer ACM-issued with managed renewal) and replace it on its listeners.
risk: If the certificate's key leaks, an attacker could impersonate the service indefinitely.

name: IoT device certificate past its rotation window
fix: Rotate device certificates (fleet provisioning / just-in-time registration) and deactivate old ones.
risk: If extracted from a device, the certificate impersonates it until someone revokes it by hand.
about: Your secret scanner matched this secret's material in code or logs; the secret is not scheduled for deletion.

name: Exposed secret is still live
fix: Rotate the secret immediately and remove it from the exposed location.
risk: Exposed-but-live secrets can be copied and used outside normal controls.
about: Your secret scanner matched this secret's material in code or logs; the secret is not scheduled for deletion.

name: Hardcoded secrets in Lambda env vars
fix: Rotate the exposed secret, move it to Secrets Manager / SSM SecureString and read it at runtime with the execution role.
risk: Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration (and every log line that dumps env) can read the secret.

name: Multiple active access keys
fix: Finish the rotation: switch consumers to one key, deactivate and delete the other.
risk: Doubles the exposure of long-lived credentials and hides which key is really in use.

name: Secret not rotated
fix: Enable automatic rotation with a rotation Lambda, or rotate manually and set a rotation schedule.
risk: A long-lived secret that leaked once stays usable indefinitely.

name: Excessive STS session duration
fix: Lower MaxSessionDuration to 1h (3600) unless a longer session is required.
risk: Stolen session credentials stay valid for many hours after the theft.

name: Secret access by non-consumers
fix: Restrict the secret's resource policy / KMS key to the intended consumers and investigate the extra readers.
risk: The secret is used outside its intended workload: over-broad access or credential misuse.

name: Privileged container / host namespace
fix: Remove privileged:true, extra Linux capabilities, pidMode/networkMode host; use awsvpc networking and task roles.
risk: Privileged containers can escape to the host, read other tasks' credentials and the EC2 instance role via IMDS.
about: The task definition grants host-level access:

name: Pod uses node role (no IRSA/Pod Identity)
fix: Create a dedicated IAM role per service account via IRSA or EKS Pod Identity and block IMDS from pods (hop limit 1).
risk: Every pod on the node shares the node role; one compromised pod gets all of its permissions.

name: Shared execution role across many functions
fix: Give each function (or each tightly related group) its own least-privilege execution role.
risk: Compromising any one function exposes the permissions of every function sharing the role.

name: SageMaker notebook direct internet
fix: Set DirectInternetAccess=Disabled and route traffic through the VPC with VPC endpoints / NAT controls.
risk: Data exfiltration path that bypasses VPC egress controls and logging.
about: DirectInternetAccess is Enabled: the notebook reaches the internet without your VPC controls, and its execution role can be used to exfiltrate data.

name: CodeBuild privileged mode
fix: Disable privileged mode unless the project builds images; for image builds use a separate project with a minimal role.
risk: Malicious build input (dependency, PR) can escape the build container and steal the project's service role credentials.
about: environment.privilegedMode=true gives build containers root on the build host (Docker daemon access).

name: Public EKS API endpoint
fix: Enable private endpoint access and disable public access, or restrict publicAccessCidrs to known ranges.
risk: Internet-exposed control plane widens the attack surface for stolen IRSA / node credentials.
about: The Kubernetes API endpoint accepts connections from 0.0.0.0/0. Leaked tokens or kubeconfigs can be used from anywhere.

name: Pod uses default service account
fix: Create a dedicated service account per workload, set automountServiceAccountToken: false on 'default'.
risk: No per-workload identity: permissions granted for one workload silently apply to all of them.
about: The pod runs as service account 'default'. Every workload in the namespace without an explicit service account shares its RBAC rights and IRSA role.

name: New sensitive-resource access
fix: Confirm the access is part of an approved change; otherwise contain the identity and review data access logs.
risk: Possible data discovery / exfiltration with the workload's credentials.

name: New API action for identity
fix: Review the calls (CloudTrail); if not a deployment change, contain the identity.
risk: Workloads are repetitive; new actions often mean reconnaissance or misuse of stolen credentials.

name: AccessDenied spike
fix: Review the denied calls in CloudTrail and contain the identity if they are not a known bug.
risk: Permission probing: someone is testing what the stolen credentials can do.

name: Impossible travel / concurrent origins
fix: Revoke active sessions and rotate the credentials; investigate the second origin.
risk: The same workload credential is being used by someone else in parallel.

name: New IP/region usage
fix: Verify the activity; if unexpected, revoke sessions (aws:TokenIssueTime deny) and rotate credentials.
risk: Workload credentials used from an unexpected location are a strong sign of theft.

name: Policy drift from baseline
fix: Confirm the change came through IaC/review; revert otherwise and alert on IAM policy changes.
risk: Unreviewed permission growth (or an attacker granting itself access).

name: Off-hours activity
fix: Correlate with deployments/batch schedules; investigate if unexplained.
risk: Attackers often use stolen credentials when nobody is watching.
about: Activity outside the identity's usual schedule.

name: Dormant-then-active credential
fix: Verify the owner expected this use; otherwise revoke and rotate.
risk: Forgotten credentials coming back to life are a classic sign of compromise.

name: Activity volume spike
fix: Check the top actions in the window; contain the identity if the spike is not explained by a release/load.
risk: Bulk enumeration or data extraction with the workload's credentials.

name: Console login by NHI
fix: Deny sts:GetFederationToken / signin for NHIs and investigate the sessions.
risk: Interactive use of workload credentials (federation via GetFederationToken / stolen keys).
about: ConsoleLogin / GetSigninToken events for a non-human identity: its credentials are being used interactively.

name: Roles Anywhere broad cert mapping
fix: Add conditions on aws:PrincipalTag/x509Subject/CN (and aws:SourceArn = the trust anchor ARN).
risk: Any certificate issued by any trusted CA in the account can obtain this role.
about: The trust policy trusts rolesanywhere.amazonaws.com without aws:PrincipalTag/x509Subject, x509Issuer or aws:SourceArn (trust anchor) conditions.

name: Wildcard OIDC/SAML subject/audience
fix: Add StringEquals conditions on <provider>:sub and <provider>:aud (SAML:aud for SAML) with exact values.
risk: Any identity issued by the provider (other apps, other tenants) can assume the role.

name: aws-auth maps broad IAM principals
fix: Map specific roles only, never account root or wildcards; give admin to a break-glass role via access entries.
risk: Many AWS principals (or long-lived user keys) get Kubernetes access, often cluster-admin.

name: Role usable without MFA condition
fix: Add Condition Bool aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent=true (or restrict aws:PrincipalArn to automation roles).
risk: Stolen long-term user keys are enough to assume this NHI role.

name: IRSA trust with wildcard subject
fix: Use StringEquals <oidc>:sub = system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<serviceaccount> and <oidc>:aud = sts.amazonaws.com.
risk: Any pod in the cluster (any namespace) can assume the role.

name: Certificate expiring/expired
fix: Renew (or enable managed renewal with DNS validation); delete expired certificates not in use.
risk: Expired certificates break TLS / mutual-TLS workload authentication (outages, fallback to insecure paths).

name: Orphaned IAM role
fix: Confirm with the owner, then delete the role (and its instance profiles).
risk: Unowned roles keep permissions and trust nobody monitors; attractive for persistence.

name: Unused OIDC/SAML provider
fix: Delete the provider if no longer needed.
risk: Leftover federation trust can be reused silently by a new or modified role.
about: No role trust policy references this provider.

name: Role last used in a region nobody watches
fix: Investigate the use; block unused regions with an SCP (aws:RequestedRegion).
risk: An unused region keeps the attacker off the dashboards and alarms the team watches.

name: Zombie credential (post-termination)
fix: Find the caller in CloudTrail, revoke sessions (deny aws:TokenIssueTime < now), and delete the role if unneeded.
risk: Credentials of a terminated workload (or exfiltrated session tokens) are still in use.

name: Unused IAM role
fix: Remove the role from the workload or reduce it to no permissions; delete when confirmed.
risk: Unused standing permissions: the workload no longer needs AWS access, or never did.

name: SSM document shared publicly/cross-account
fix: Remove public sharing (ModifyDocumentPermission --account-ids-to-remove all) and unneeded accounts.
risk: Leaks operational details and any secrets embedded in the document.
about: The automation/command document is visible outside your organization; documents often embed scripts, endpoints and parameter names.

name: Public/broad resource policy (invoke)
fix: Restrict the permission to the calling service with aws:SourceArn / aws:SourceAccount, or to specific principals.
risk: Outsiders can trigger the function and act with its execution role.
about: The function's resource policy grants lambda:InvokeFunction (or broader) to

name: Snapshot shared publicly/cross-account
fix: Remove 'all' and unneeded accounts from the restore attribute; encrypt snapshots with a CMK not shared externally.
risk: A complete copy of the database, including credentials tables and PII.
about: The snapshot's restore attribute lets other accounts (or everyone) restore a full copy of the database.

name: Bucket policy broad/public
fix: Enable S3 Block Public Access, remove public statements and AllUsers grants, restrict cross-account access with aws:PrincipalOrgID.
risk: Bucket contents can be read (or written) by anyone / outside your organization.

name: Layer shared cross-account with secrets
fix: Rotate the secrets, rebuild the layer without them, remove public/cross-account layer permissions.
risk: Anyone allowed to use the layer can download it and extract the credentials.

name: EventBridge bus open to anyone or unknown accounts
fix: Restrict the bus policy to known accounts or aws:PrincipalOrgID.
risk: An outsider can inject events that trigger your rules and the targets (and roles) behind them.
about: The event bus policy grants Principal \

name: Function URL with no auth
fix: Set AuthType=AWS_IAM, or put the function behind API Gateway / CloudFront with authentication.
risk: Internet-reachable entry point running with the function's execution role.
about: The function URL accepts unauthenticated HTTPS requests from the internet.

name: Bucket readable by all authenticated AWS
fix: Remove the AuthenticatedUsers grant, set Object Ownership to BucketOwnerEnforced (disables ACLs).
risk: Anyone with a free AWS account can access the bucket.
about: The 'AuthenticatedUsers' group means ANY AWS account, not just yours.
